newsitem.title: USA: SEC charges former PaineWebber broker.
newsitem.headline: SEC charges former PaineWebber broker.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said Tuesday that it has filed a complaint against a former PaineWebber Group Inc broker and a lawyer, charging them with insider trading.

The complaint alleged that James D'Angelo, who worked as a stockbroker at PaineWebber's Andover, Mass. branch, bought common stock of BayBanks Inc in December, 1995 while in possession of nonpublic information about its impending acquisition by BankBoston Corp.

The complaint further alleged that D'Angelo obtained the information through a tip from John Larrabee, who was the director of fiduciary services at Bingham, Dana & Gould, a Boston law firm that represented BankBoston in the acquisition.

After receiving the tip, D'Angelo bought 10,200 shares of BayBanks on Dec 12, 1995 at $85 a share for a total of $867,000 through his own brokerage account and through accounts controlled by his ex-wife, children, grandchild and girlfriend, the complaint alleged.
The purchase was his first of BayBanks stock and represented about 20 percent of that day's trading volume in BayBanks stock.
The banks announced an agreement valued at $2 billion in stock to merge that day. The next day, D'Angelo sold the shares for a profit of $86,750.

The SEC said that D'Angelo agreed to pay, pending approval by a court, disgorgement of $86,750 plus prejudgment interest in the amount of $8,552 and a civil penalty of $86,750 for a total of $182,052.
D'Angelo, who did not admit or deny the allegations, agreed to be barred from having any association with any broker, dealer or investment company.
